chosen_leak: In-app entry: arrived in the create app -> picked a role -> started creating a video (index.html welcome/role-pick). ~62% of warm, email-having users never reach 'Create' (PostHog 30d: page_view 190 -> Create Video Button Clicked 72 = 38%), and the single biggest sub-drop is at the very first screen, arrived -> picked a role (~44%).
why_highest_impact: Traced to REVIEWS, this beats the other open leaks. Reviews are the only goal, and 81% of review clicks (17 of 21 in the last 30d Supabase report) come from the in-app THANK-YOU screen, which only appears AFTER a video is finished; email reminders produced just 2, preview/share 2. So the dominant review tap is gated entirely by getting warm users through the in-app entry to a finished video. These users are the warmest in the funnel: they already paid the email price and were auto-forwarded in (~97%), so this is a pure motivation/UX problem with no gate or exchange to protect. The email gate (landed->email, ~58% loss) is bigger by raw headcount and sits higher in the funnel, but it is disqualified on two counts: (1) RECENCY - it was genuinely attacked TWICE just 9 days ago (2026-07-23 warm-voice rewrite + character-portrait hero) on top of PR #8, making it exactly the 'recently-touched biggest leak' the brief says not to reach for; (2) its marginal review value per recovered scanner is diluted - many are one-off gift buyers who will never place the 'next order' the discount rewards, and the reminder-email path they would feed yields only ~10% of review clicks. Meanwhile the in-app entry was last touched 2026-06-16 (one mechanism, the value-prop hero, whose contribution was never even isolated) and the occasion/examples screen inside it has NEVER been touched - so a large, high-leverage, warm-traffic leak that directly gates 81% of reviews is genuinely under-worked. Remaining leaks rank below it: preview/share review asks (~2 of 21 clicks, low volume, already attacked in June), Klaviyo reminder emails (out of repo scope), and the box/insert (fixed print, cannot change).

angles.angle: Payoff-first hero: a captioned, sound-off example that sells itself
angles.mechanism: Replace the muted, controls-hidden welcome clip that requires a 'Tap for sound' to mean anything with a finished example video as the dominant above-the-fold element, auto-playing with the punchline BAKED IN as on-screen captions so the emotional payoff lands with the phone on mute (the default state of QR/mobile traffic). Answer 'why would I make one of these?' by showing the delightful result before the role fork, instead of describing it.
angles.cause_addressed: Unclear / unfelt value: the video is an UNANNOUNCED bonus (never promised on the box), and the one asset that could convey its magic plays silently, so most users never feel the payoff and see no reason to do the work.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: #welcomeVideo autoplays muted with a 'Tap for sound' overlay and hidden controls; PostHog fires a separate 'Welcome Video - Tapped For Sound' event, so a low tap rate would confirm most users experience the demo silently. Grounded, with a sound-tap-rate check to firm it up.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The only prior in-app-entry attempt (2026-06-16) was a TEXT value-prop hero (a benefit headline + a 'Free / Takes a minute / No app needed' cost line). This is not a reworded headline - it is a visual-demonstration change (captioned auto-playing result as the hero). It is on index.html, so it is unrelated to the claim-page 07-23 imagery/voice work and to every owner rejection.
angles.on_brand_fit: Premium and warm: leads with a real, affectionate result rather than emoji claims; captions replace the busy 'Tap for sound' affordance, cleaning up the first paint.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: swaps the welcome hero media + adds baked-in captions and removes the sound-tap overlay dependency; touches the welcome section only, no step removed, no gate/reward touched.

angles.mechanism: The claim-user welcome currently OPENS with the loudest possible reason to leave: 'YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY / We sent your code to {email} / Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder.' That both signals 'you already have what you came for' and literally instructs the user to switch to their email app - a competing CTA at the exact moment we need them to stay. Demote this to a slim, calm one-line confirmation strip (keep the reassurance, never remove it) and lead the screen with the invitation to create, so the first and loudest thing is the video, not 'go check your email'.
angles.cause_addressed: Wrong timing + no reason to continue: a self-inflicted competing call-to-action pulls warm users out of the funnel at arrival and tells them they are already done.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map, lines ~1620-1642: the claim-arrival header is rewritten to lead with the code-status + 'Check your spam folder' block ABOVE the 'who are you?' prompt. This is an observable structural flaw at the top of the ~44% arrived->role drop, not a guess about feelings.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Untouched since the 2026-06-16 hero; that attempt ADDED a value-prop, it never addressed the reassurance block competing with the ask. Distinct from the claim-page 07-23 voice change (different page, different content) and from every owner rejection (nothing about codes-before-email or the printed %).
angles.on_brand_fit: Refined, not pushy: it keeps the honest reassurance the user needs but restores a calm visual hierarchy - one quiet confirmation line, one clear invitation - which is more premium than the current stacked eyebrows and emoji.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: re-ranks and slims the existing claim-welcome header block; keeps all reassurance copy, removes no step, changes no reward or delivery path.

angles.mechanism: The screen frames video creation as idle filler ('While you wait...'), the weakest possible motivation. Reframe the ask around a concrete, warm occasion the gift creates - a surprise to send WITH or BEFORE the gift arrives, or a keepsake the receiver will love - so making it reads as a purposeful moment, not a way to kill time until an email lands.
angles.cause_addressed: Thin motivation / no reason to act now: 'while you wait' actively tells the user this is optional time-filler, so there is nothing lost by closing the tab.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: the claim-welcome literally uses a 'While you wait...' eyebrow before the video headline. Unsettled on magnitude - a bet on motivation framing - but the anti-motivation wording is directly in the code.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The 2026-06-16 hero STATED a benefit ('a video they'll love') and listed cost; this changes the PURPOSE/urgency framing of the act itself (occasion-anchored reason vs benefit statement) - a different mechanism, and it targets the 'while you wait' line the hero never touched.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm and human: ties into the gift's real emotional moment in the box's playful register, no pressure, no incentive-for-review language.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: rewrites the eyebrow + lead-in on the welcome section; no layout rebuild, no step or reward change.

angles.angle: Warm the role fork: choose an outcome, not an identity
angles.mechanism: The first interaction is a cold identity fork - two glass cards asking 'who are you? buyer or receiver?' before any value is felt. Redesign the two choice cards to be larger, warmer, and OUTCOME-framed: each card previews what that person makes (receiver -> 'a thank-you they'll love'; buyer -> 'a surprise before it arrives'), optionally carrying the crochet character thumbnail, so the tap reads as choosing a delightful result rather than classifying yourself.
angles.cause_addressed: Decision friction / confusion at the fork: an abstract identity question with no felt reward is a poor first ask, and the single biggest sub-drop sits exactly here.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: role-pick is one tap on .choice-card with terse labels ('I Received This Gift' / 'I'm Giving This Gift') and small emoji; changelog baseline puts the heaviest first-screen loss at arrived->role. Where taps stop is visible in session replay.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The 2026-06-16 hero lived ABOVE the cards and never restyled the CHOICE itself; the cards have no lever/experiment annotation in the code (unlike the hero and thank-you screen). Different surface, different mechanism (the decision UI, not the pitch).
angles.on_brand_fit: Premium: bigger tap targets, real imagery, warm outcome language, fewer decorative emoji - a cleaner, more confident fork than the current small cards.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: restyles the two existing .choice-card elements and their copy/imagery; both roles remain, nothing removed.

angles.angle: Use the role we already know: confirm, don't re-ask
angles.mechanism: The claim URL already carries ?branch=, but the app discards it and forces a fresh role pick ('Let claim users start at welcome screen'). When branch is present and reliable, pre-select the likely role and present a single warm primary action ('Yes - let's make it') with an easy, visible 'actually, I'm the other one' switch, collapsing a two-way fork into a one-tap confirm. The role is still chosen (no step removed), just defaulted.
angles.cause_addressed: Friction: an extra, redundant decision at the highest-drop screen when the answer is already known upstream.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: DOMContentLoaded reads ?branch= into userType yet still lands on welcome and requires a re-tap (comment confirms). Whether branch is reliably set for claim traffic is unsettled - a bet to validate before build.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Never attempted; unrelated to the 2026-06-16 hero (a pitch change, not a flow change) and to any owner rejection. It reduces a decision without removing the role step or any gate/reward.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm and effortless: greeting the user with 'we think this gift is for you...' feels considerate and premium, and the always-visible switch keeps it honest and non-coercive.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: adds a pre-selected default + confirm/switch on the existing role UI, gated behind a reliable branch value; both roles stay reachable, no step removed.

angles.angle: Endowed-progress: show they're two quick steps from done
angles.mechanism: Warm users overestimate the effort of 'making a video' and bail before starting. Add a subtle, premium progress cue at the top of the entry flow (e.g. a slim 'Step 1 of 2' / 'nearly there' stepper) so the task visibly looks almost finished. People complete what appears close to done - an endowed-progress mechanism that lowers perceived effort without changing the actual steps.
angles.cause_addressed: Overestimated effort: 'create an AI video' sounds like real work, so warm users abandon at arrival rather than start something long.
angles.evidence_hint: Unsettled - a bet. Effort perception is a classic abandon driver; very-short-dwell exits on the welcome screen in session replay would support it. Note: the occasion screens already show a lone 'Step 1' eyebrow, so a coherent stepper is a natural, low-risk addition.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The 2026-06-16 hero addressed value, not perceived length; no progress/commitment affordance has ever been added to the entry flow. Structural mechanism, distinct from any copy or imagery attempt.
angles.on_brand_fit: Minimal and refined: a quiet type-based stepper fits the clean hierarchy bar and avoids emoji or hype.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: adds a small progress indicator across welcome->role->create; no step added or removed, no reward change.

angles.angle: Name their crochet friend: make the ask about THIS gift
angles.mechanism: The welcome screen speaks generically ('turn your gift into a video'), while the specific character they bought - already resolvable from the SKU - stays a background prop. Bring the exact crochet friend to the foreground of the welcome ask by name and image ('Let's bring your Green Potato to life for them'), so the invitation feels personal and about their real gift, not a generic app they were dumped into.
angles.cause_addressed: Weak emotional / personal connection: a generic pitch right after a warm, handmade-gift moment feels like a context switch into an unrelated tool, sapping the affection that would motivate creating.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: updateWelcomeVideo/updateProductImages already swap MEDIA per product, but the headline/framing stay product-agnostic; the SKU and character are known on load. Grounded that the data exists; the connection effect is the bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Distinct from the claim-page character-portrait work (2026-07-23, different page) and from the 2026-06-16 generic hero (this personalizes the COPY/framing to the named character, not a generic benefit). No owner rejection touches personalization.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm and premium: naming the handmade friend continues the box's affectionate voice and centers the craft, without hype or emoji soup.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: personalizes the welcome headline/framing using the already-resolved SKU/character; no new fetch, no step or reward change.

pick_rationale: It wins on value x confidence x on-brand fit. Value: it attacks the most direct, observable cause of the biggest sub-drop (arrived -> role, ~44% of the warmest users) - at arrival the loudest content literally tells the user their code is handled and points them at their email app, a competing CTA that both removes the reason to continue and invites a physical exit. Recovering even a slice of these users flows straight into the 81% review path (finished video -> thank-you screen). Confidence: unlike the higher-ceiling bets, this is not a hypothesis about feelings - the flawed block is right there in the claim-welcome markup, and the fix (demote reassurance, lead with the invitation) is small and reversible, so it is buildable and low-risk even at our noise-floor traffic. On-brand: it keeps every honest reassurance the user needs while restoring a calm, premium hierarchy - more refined than today's stacked eyebrows and emoji. It beats the runners-up: 'Payoff-first hero' (Angle 1) has a higher ceiling and is the strongest alternative the planner may prefer, but it is a bigger build (a captioned asset) and a larger bet on value demonstration; 'Reason-to-act' and 'Name their crochet friend' are cheaper but rest more on unproven motivation framing; 'Pre-select the role' hinges on unverified branch reliability. Cleanly distinct from the one fenced mechanism here (the 2026-06-16 value-prop hero) and from every owner rejection.
